meta.status: Prototype. Every row needs review and sign-off by the D7 owner before client use.
meta.howToRead: One row per catalogue use case (ids = department id + position in the catalogue, the same ids the readiness tool uses). base = label when no deciding question is answered yes. switches = the questions that can change the label (soft = asked, but does not make the label conditional while unanswered; src research = added from desk research, not in the booklet). a6 = how the booklet page A6 counts the use (high, highif, transp, prohib). booklet = where the booklet states it. review = points for the D7 owner.

uses.name: Demand forecasting (rooms, by day/segment/room class)
Dynamic pricing & rate optimisation (incl. autopilot publishing)
uses.why: Dynamic pricing and forecasting are not on the Act's list of high-risk uses. Consumer and competition law bite harder on prices.
uses.prov: Not on the Annex III list

uses.name: Competitor rate shopping & market intelligence with ML
GenAI RM copilots & BI Q&A / price explanations
Agentic revenue management (agents that monitor, recommend and act)
Revenue, budget & total-revenue forecasting (incl. function space, beyond rooms)
Upsell & ancillary price optimisation
Spa and wellness yield management and dynamic treatment pricing
AI voice agents for reservation and front-desk calls (property line and central reservations)
uses.why: It talks to callers, so they must be told it is AI. Switching on an emotion or voiceprint feature would make it high-risk.

uses.name: Email & offer reservation handling with LLMs
AI channel management / ARI distribution
Booking-engine AI assistant & personalisation
uses.why: It talks to guests on the booking engine, so they must be told it is AI.

uses.name: Cancellation / no-show prediction & overbooking optimisation
Group rooming lists, rate loading & reservation operations (GenAI/agentic)
Bookable hotel apps in AI assistants (ChatGPT apps, MCP servers)
uses.review: Not analysed in the booklet: AI assistants that book on a guest's behalf (desk research, 17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: AI call scoring and conversation analytics for reservation calls
uses.why: It scores individual reservation agents' calls, which is monitoring and evaluating staff.

uses.name: GenAI marketing text content & translation
uses.why: AI-written marketing text is minimal. Health, safety or sustainability claims published without human review must be disclosed as AI-written.

uses.name: Group/MICE enquiry intake & RFP/proposal response
CRM segmentation, predictive targeting, loyalty & personalised email campaigns
GenAI imagery & video for marketing
uses.why: AI images and video are minimal unless they are realistic and could mislead about the hotel.

uses.name: Paid media, metasearch & programmatic optimisation
SEO / AI-search (GEO) visibility & AI-assistant distribution
Lead qualification, scoring & prospecting (group/MICE and B2B)
Digital check-in with ID document capture (online/mobile/kiosk)
AI room assignment
uses.review: The booklet row "Room assignment and cleaning plans" mixes this guest-facing use with housekeeping assignment (hk-6).

uses.name: Biometric face verification at check-in (selfie-to-ID 1:1 match)
uses.why: Matching a guest's selfie to their own ID document is verification, which the Act's biometric category expressly excludes. Face data is still the most protected kind of personal data.
uses.review: The booklet marks this "(draft guidance)". The exclusion is in the text of Annex III 1(a) itself (text check, 17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: Front-desk copilots and PMS AI agents
Upsell at check-in (desk, kiosk, pre-arrival)
Review analysis and sentiment / guest-feedback analytics
uses.why: Analysing the text of reviews or messages is not emotion recognition and stays allowed.

uses.name: AI chat and messaging assistant, pre-booking and in-stay (web, WhatsApp, OTA inbox; multilingual)
uses.why: It chats with guests, so they must be told it is AI in its first message.

uses.name: GenAI review response
Guest personalisation from unified guest profile
In-stay digital concierge and recommendations
uses.why: A digital concierge talks to guests, so they must be told it is AI.

uses.name: In-room voice assistant
uses.why: It talks to guests, so they must be told it is AI. Reading guests' emotions from their voice would make it high-risk.

uses.name: Event and banqueting sales AI (leads, proposals, contracts)
In-room dining and outlet ordering via chat/voice assistants
uses.why: Ordering bots talk to guests, so they must say they are AI.

uses.name: Menu engineering and F&B pricing optimisation
QR / mobile ordering with AI upselling and dynamic menu pricing
Room-delivery and service robots (amenities, room service, outlets)
uses.why: A service robot must say it is AI only if it talks to guests and is not obviously a machine.

uses.name: Restaurant table reservations: voice AI and AI table management
uses.why: A table-booking phone agent talks to guests, so it must say it is AI.

uses.name: Multilingual task capture and staff messaging (voice/chat to task, translation)
Autonomous cleaning robots (floor care)
uses.why: Minimal for the hotel. Robots are machinery: product safety is the maker's matter, so ask the maker for the CE mark.
uses.review: The booklet groups robots with gas appliances. After the July 2026 amendment, machinery sits in Annex I Section B (desk research, 17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: Linen and amenity forecasting / RFID linen tracking
Occupancy-sensor driven cleaning and room status
Room inspection with computer vision
uses.why: Minimal if findings go only to the attendant. High-risk if results are used to judge individual attendants.

uses.name: Room-cleaning prioritisation, assignment and workload optimisation
uses.why: Minimal if it allocates by room status and availability. High-risk if it ranks attendants by speed or ratings, or reports rooms per hour on each attendant to supervisors.

uses.name: AI HVAC / BMS optimisation and energy analytics (central plant)
uses.why: AI that only optimises energy, comfort or efficiency is not a safety component, unless its failure would endanger people.

uses.name: Work-order triage, creation and asset register
Digital twins
Guest-room energy management (occupancy-based HVAC/lighting)
Predictive maintenance - OEM-connected equipment (lifts, escalators, doors)
uses.why: Predicting maintenance needs is minimal. AI that is part of a lift's safety function, such as door and obstacle detection, is high-risk from 2 Aug 2028, and that is the lift maker's duty.
uses.review: A6 counts lift-door safety AI here, while the catalogue use is predictive maintenance, which Art. 6(1a) carves out (desk research, 17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: Predictive maintenance - hotel-run across assets (HVAC, kitchen, technical devices)
uses.why: Predicting maintenance needs is minimal. Hotel-run safety AI for gas or pressure equipment (rare) would be high-risk from 2 Aug 2028 and would make the group its maker.
uses.review: A6 counts hotel-run gas or pressure safety AI here, while the catalogue use is predictive maintenance (desk research, 17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: Water leak and fault detection
Food-waste measurement with computer vision
uses.why: Minimal when it measures food. High-risk if footage or logs are used to rate individual cooks. Kitchen cameras film staff as well as food, so labour law applies either way.

uses.name: Allergen handling and menu labelling
Intelligent cooking equipment (ovens that recognise the food)
uses.why: Minimal for the hotel; ask the maker. AI that controls gas appliances can be a safety component from 2 Aug 2028.

uses.name: Production, covers and breakfast-buffet forecasting (incl. purchasing quantities)
Recipe and menu generation (GenAI)
Automated purchase recommendations / reordering
Demand & inventory forecasting for purchasing
Invoice-to-PO matching (2/3-way) & invoice error detection
Spend analytics & stock-variance / shrink detection
uses.why: AI used only to protect the hotel's property is not high-risk. Using the same alerts to judge individual staff can make it so.

uses.name: Supplier price comparison, benchmarking & contract-price compliance
Supplier price forecasting for negotiations
AP invoice capture & GL coding (OCR/ML)
Fraud / anomaly detection in payments
uses.why: Fraud detection is not on the Act's high-risk list; it is expressly excluded from the credit-scoring category.

uses.name: Automated reconciliation (bank, card, OTA commission, PMS, supplier statement)
Cash-flow, P&L forecasting & budgeting
GenAI finance copilots & AP agents
Night audit automation
Chargeback dispute automation
Labour demand forecasting and scheduling (all departments, incl. housekeeping attendants)
uses.why: Minimal if it forecasts demand or allocates shifts on stated availability. High-risk if it ranks staff, significantly changes regular hours or decides leave.
uses.kw: rota roster shift planning workforce management

uses.name: AI recruiting (conversational hiring, screening, matching)
uses.why: Tools that screen, rank or match job applicants are on the Act's high-risk list. A hiring chatbot must also say it is AI.
uses.kw: CV screening ATS video interview applicant tracking

uses.name: Onboarding and training (GenAI course creation, AI coaching, microlearning)
uses.why: Minimal for creating courses and coaching. High-risk if its assessments decide pay, promotion or continued employment.
uses.review: Desk research adds a second route: Annex III point 3 for hotel schools and academies (17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: Retention and attrition prediction, engagement analytics
uses.why: Minimal as a forecast. High-risk if used to decide renewals, promotions or dismissals.
uses.review: "Minimal as a forecast" may be over-confident for scores on named individuals (desk research, 17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: Seasonal staff matching to properties
uses.why: Matching seasonal staff to properties decides who gets which work (our reading).

uses.name: BI and KPI dashboards with AI analysis
uses.why: Minimal for business figures. High-risk if the dashboards rank individual staff.

uses.name: GenAI copilots and enterprise assistants for managers and corporate staff
uses.why: A general assistant is minimal for everyday work. Using it to rank applicants or judge staff is a high-risk use and can make the hotel the tool's maker (our reading).
uses.kw: ChatGPT Copilot Gemini Claude general chatbot

uses.name: Meeting, briefing and report automation
Enterprise AI and data platforms at hotel groups
Owner and asset-manager reporting
Frontline staff knowledge assistant (handbook and SOP questions)
AI threat detection and autonomous response (network, email, endpoint)
AI IT service desk
uses.review: The catalogue lists "sentiment, speech analytics" on staff calls, which would be emotion recognition at work (desk research, 17 Nov 2026).

uses.name: Booking fraud detection (reservation, OTA-impersonation and card-not-present fraud at booking)
uses.why: Fraud detection is not on the Act's high-risk list; it is expressly excluded from the credit-scoring category.

uses.name: Physical security video analytics
uses.why: Minimal for intrusion, object or occupancy detection. Recognising guests at a distance or reading crowd mood is high-risk; reading staff emotions or inferring sensitive traits is prohibited.

uses.name: AI network operations for guest and staff Wi-Fi
ESG / carbon data collection and reporting
GDPR / data-request handling and AI Act compliance tooling
GenAI contract review and legal assistance
AI use policies and governance
uses.why: A governance document, not an AI tool.

uses.name: Guest screening and risk scoring before arrival
uses.why: Minimal by default. It is the hotel use closest to the ban on social scoring: scores built on data from unrelated contexts that lead to refusing guests. Data protection law on automated decisions applies today.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Shared banned-guest or "do not rent" databases
uses.why: Often a plain database, which is not an AI system. If an AI score is added, it comes close to the ban on social scoring. Matching banned guests by face on cameras is high-risk.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: AI avatar or hologram receptionist
uses.why: It talks to guests, so it must say it is AI. A realistic avatar or human-like voice does not count as obviously a machine.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: AI video or voice interviews for hiring
uses.why: Analysing or ranking candidates in interviews is recruitment, which is on the Act's high-risk list. Reading their emotions from face or voice is prohibited.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Staff panic buttons and location wearables
uses.why: Usually a button and a location beacon, which is not AI. Used only for safety, it stays outside the high-risk list. High-risk if location or dwell data is reused to judge attendants.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Per-attendant productivity dashboards (minutes per room)
uses.why: A plain report of timestamps may not be AI. Where AI predicts or scores each attendant, it is high-risk. This is the feature the booklet warns about for housekeeping tools.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Biometric staff time clocks (face or fingerprint)
uses.why: Checking a worker against their own stored template is verification, which the Act's biometric category excludes. Data protection law decides, and it is strict.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Noise, occupancy, smoking and vape sensors in rooms
uses.prov: Not on the Annex III list
uses.why: No biometric identification and not on the high-risk list. Many are threshold devices and may not be AI. Data protection law on monitoring a private room, and consumer law on automatic fees, are the real issues.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Weapon, aggression and behaviour detection on cameras and audio
uses.why: Detecting an object such as a weapon is minimal. Detecting aggression or anger from gestures, face or voice sits on the line of emotion recognition, which is high-risk for guests and prohibited for staff.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: AI drowning detection in pools
uses.prov: Not on the Annex III list
uses.why: Not on the high-risk list, and a stand-alone camera system is not a safety part of a regulated product (our reading). Product liability and the hotel's duty of care matter more.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Licence-plate recognition for hotel parking
uses.prov: Not on the Annex III list
uses.why: A number plate is not biometric data, so this is minimal. Data protection law applies.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Facial age estimation at self-service alcohol points
uses.why: Estimating age from a face sorts people by a biometric trait, so the people exposed must be told. Age is not a sensitive attribute, so the use is not high-risk (draft guidance).
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Spa and wellness AI: skin analysis, body scans, sleep tracking
uses.why: Minimal unless the product is a medical device. Sorting guests by skin or face analysis brings a notice duty, and reading mood or stress from face or voice is high-risk. Body and sleep data are health data today.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Robot cooks and automated food stations
uses.why: Minimal for the hotel. Robots are machinery: product safety is the maker's matter, so ask the maker for the CE mark.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Tip pooling and gratuity distribution software
uses.why: Mostly rules-based today, which is not AI. If an AI model sets each person's share from their performance, it decides pay and is high-risk.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Real-time translation devices and accessibility aids at the desk
uses.why: Translation and transcription tools do not have to announce themselves as AI (Commission guidance).
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.

uses.name: Smart minibars with automatic billing
uses.why: Infrared and switch sensors follow fixed rules, so this is not an AI system. Consumer law on automatic charges applies.
uses.review: Not in the team's catalogue of 91. Found in vendor material and trade press by desk research (17 Nov 2026, search summaries). Provisional label, not yet reviewed by the team.
